clue.text: Crash at speed and it's broken

definitions.text: Crash at speed and it's broken

parts.words: Crash at speed and it's broken
parts.note: the 'crash' is the loud bang an aircraft makes when it passes the speed of sound, and that limit is what gets broken

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a high-speed accident that breaks something; in fact the crash is a sonic boom and what is broken is the limit itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft going supersonic are said to break this barrier, producing a sonic boom.

clue.text: Examination as soon as it's finished

definitions.meaning: the moment something is done, read as two words

explanation.definitionFit: A quick check is a once-over; 'once' meaning when and 'over' meaning ended also give as soon as it's done.

clue.text: They're rumoured to open doors for posh folk

indicators.note: something rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word that sounds like another

parts.note: door handles you turn to open doors are knobs

explanation.surface: Servants who open doors for the upper classes, it is said.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobs is British slang for wealthy, upper-class people, the toffs.

clue.text: Adds herbal remedy, though it's nonsense!

indicators.note: a remedy puts something right, so these letters are fixed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone scoffing that adding a herbal remedy is rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remedy' looks like part of the herbal medicine phrase but is the anagram signal on ADDS HERBAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Balderdash is a dated word for foolish talk or rubbish.

clue.text: Fruit that is caught in shower

indicators.note: something caught in another thing is held inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a shower is a short fall of rain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A piece of fruit left out in a downpour.
explanation.definitionFit: A raisin is a dried grape, a kind of dried fruit.

clue.text: Batting maybe perfect, with concentration

parts.note: in cricket a side that is batting is said to be in
the perfect is one example of a grammatical tense, hence 'maybe'

explanation.surface: A cricketer's flawless innings played with total focus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perfect' looks like praise for the batting but is a grammar term: the perfect is a verb tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense effort or study is done with great concentration and focus.

clue.text: Memory of soldiers gathering

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a corps of the British Army
a gathering of things is a collection

explanation.surface: Someone recalling a time when troops assembled.
explanation.definitionFit: A recollection is something remembered, a recalled event.

clue.text: Party fun beginning — is tea being served?

indicators.note: the beginning of the word fun is its opening letter
tea being served is poured out and moved about, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether tea will be offered at the start of a jolly party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' suggests tea at a party, but 'being served' is the anagram signal, and the 'beginning' of fun supplies only one letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiesta is a festive celebration, especially in Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Record is accepted by district commissioner

indicators.note: something accepted by another is taken in by it, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An official approving a written record.
explanation.definitionFit: A disc is a gramophone record, the vinyl kind played on a turntable.

clue.text: Very angry, seeing student is drowning in European sea

indicators.note: something drowning in the sea is submerged within it, so it goes inside

parts.note: the Baltic is a sea in northern Europe
L, for learner, is the usual crossword abbreviation for a student
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone furious at watching a student drowning in northern waters.
explanation.definitionFit: To go ballistic is an idiom for flying into a rage.

clue.text: Cut short to finish harvest and depart northwards

parts.note: to close something is to finish it
a harvest is a crop

indicators.note: in a down clue, going northwards means reading upwards, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: dep is the abbreviation for depart seen on timetables

explanation.surface: A farmer cutting the harvest short and heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'northwards' reverses DEP, the timetable abbreviation, to give PED.
explanation.definitionFit: Hair or grass that is close-cropped has been trimmed very short.

clue.text: Damage insole running

indicators.note: running shoes take a battering, and the letters of the word insole are jumbled about

explanation.surface: A runner's shoe lining has been worn through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running' is the anagram signal on INSOLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A lesion is an injury or harmful change in body tissue.

clue.text: Individual working in majestic surroundings of an area

indicators.note: majestic surroundings means the word for majestic surrounds the rest

parts.note: majestic means regal
I is a single one, an individual
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Someone employed in a grand setting somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Regional describes something belonging to a particular district or territory.

clue.text: Research establishment for political party speech-making

parts.note: Lab is the abbreviation for the UK Labour Party
oratory is the art of public speaking

explanation.surface: An institute set up to study politicians' rhetoric.
explanation.definitionFit: A laboratory is a place equipped for scientific experiments.

clue.text: How to greet Sunday workers eating fish?

indicators.note: one thing eating another takes it inside, so a piece goes within

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farmhands
hake is a sea fish related to cod

explanation.surface: Weekend staff tucking into a fish lunch, with a question about greetings.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking another's right palm is a customary way of welcoming someone.

clue.text: Fine summer in France for a fair!

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
the French word for summer is ete

explanation.surface: Lovely summer weather in France, ideal for an outdoor fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fundraising event with stalls and games, like a village fair.

clue.text: Seat plan turned out to be nice enough

indicators.note: turned out suggests something rearranged or produced differently, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A seating plan for an event proves satisfactory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' looks like 'proved' but is the anagram signal on SEAT PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasant means agreeable or enjoyable, mildly nice.

clue.text: Policeman outside hotel given something to eat

indicators.note: outside means the policeman wraps around the other letter

parts.note: cop is slang for a police officer
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An officer outside a hotel being handed a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A chop is a cut of meat, often lamb or pork, for a meal.

clue.text: Get too big to see good in unfashionable argument

indicators.note: the letter for good goes in the middle of the other words

parts.note: out means no longer in fashion
a row is a noisy quarrel

explanation.surface: Someone seeing the merit of an old-fashioned dispute.
explanation.definitionFit: To outgrow something is to become too large for it, like clothes.

clue.text: Doctor and diplomat overseas go brown, with time

parts.note: a consul is a government official posted abroad
to tan is to go brown in the sun

explanation.surface: A medic and a foreign envoy sunbathing for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant is a senior hospital physician or specialist.

clue.text: The approach one takes to a meeting place

parts.note: a venue is where an event or meeting is held

explanation.surface: Asking how one should get to a conference location.
explanation.definitionFit: An avenue is a way of approaching something, a route or line of attack.

clue.text: Save first son caught on edge, parking

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a rim is an edge
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A parent saving money while their son's car is stuck on the kerb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' tells you the S comes at the front, ahead of the other pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrimp is to economise hard, putting money by.

clue.text: Go for chemical company with an outlet in the high street

parts.note: to opt for something is to go for it
ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, a major British chemical company

explanation.surface: Choosing a chemical firm that has a shop on the main street.
explanation.walkthrough: A high street is a British town's main shopping street, where an eye-test shop is a familiar sight.
explanation.definitionFit: An optician runs an eye-care shop, a familiar retail business in town centres.

clue.text: Manage to get to the party

parts.note: to make an event is to manage to attend it
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: Arranging to attend a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To make do is to cope with whatever is available.

clue.text: A rumoured purchaser for the cowshed

indicators.note: something rumoured is passed on by word of mouth, so we want a word sounding like another

parts.note: a purchaser is a buyer

explanation.surface: Gossip about someone buying a farm outbuilding.
explanation.definitionFit: A byre is a farm building where cattle are kept.

clue.text: Wages covering minors perhaps show meanness

indicators.note: covering means one piece goes around the other

parts.note: wages are pay

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the word minors might be arranged another way, so it is an anagram

explanation.surface: Paying low wages to young workers reveals stinginess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minors perhaps' looks like underage workers being paid; 'perhaps' is the anagram signal, and 'covering' puts the jumbled letters inside the pay.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsimony is extreme unwillingness to spend money, stinginess.

clue.text: Fit to contend without run

indicators.note: without means the letter for run is taken away

parts.note: to contend is to argue
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Fit enough to compete, but unable to run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' looks like healthy but is the noun: a bout of fever.
explanation.definitionFit: An ague is a fever with shivering fits, as in malaria.

clue.text: Reorganise and stop my new deposits

indicators.note: to reorganise is to arrange afresh, so these letters go into a new order

explanation.surface: Telling someone to reshuffle their finances and halt a new purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reorganise' is the anagram signal on AND STOP MY NEW.
explanation.definitionFit: Down payments are initial part-payments made when buying on credit.
